summary: Transient private-deploy maintenance surcharge applied on finalized invoice after hosted fallback
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (NimbleRetail) received a finalized invoice (period 2024-10-15 to 2024-11-14) which includes a line item labeled 'Private deployment maintenance surcharge — prorated' for €1,250. Customer asserts they did not opt into any maintenance add-on and their private deployment was on an auto-update path that completed during the billing window.

Impact:
- Invoice shows unexpected charge causing temporary hold on autopay for the account.
- Finance team at NimbleRetail requesting immediate explanation and credit reversal.
- This is blocking month-end reconciliation for the customer.

Environment:
- Customer private deployment (VPC) serving production traffic in eu-west.
- Private control plane version: v2024.10.3.
- Router/service-layer recorded a transient fallback to hosted endpoints during a cross-region capacity rebalance on 2024-10-29 03:42 UTC.

Steps to reproduce / observed timeline:
1) 2024-10-29 03:30 UTC — Autoscaler initiated capacity rebalance on dedicated gpu pool (eu-west-2).
2) 2024-10-29 03:42 UTC — Control plane recorded a 12-minute window where some requests routed to hosted fallback (hosted API) due to ephemeral scheduling mismatch.
3) 2024-10-29 03:55 UTC — Routing normalized; private endpoints restored.
4) Billing postback handler aggregated usage and later applied a prorated maintenance surcharge tag to the customer's invoice for the day of the fallback.

Observed behaviour:
- Finalized invoice includes a maintenance-surcharge line with description referencing a private deployment maintenance SKU.
- Billing ledger shows the surcharge was applied during the same window as the hosted fallback events.

Expected behaviour:
- Transient hosted fallback should not trigger private-deployment maintenance add-ons. Maintenance/ops surcharges are only billable when customer has purchased the maintenance add-on or when an explicit maintenance window was scheduled and accepted.

Logs & Evidence attached (references):
- Router logs: link to internal log stream (redacted) - channel #private-fallback-logs (Slack).
- Postback audit: billing/postback/2024-10-29/evt-88214 (internal).
- Console snapshots: Rollout history for nimbleretail-account (confluence link above).

Notes: Customer provided screenshot of invoice line and their internal purchase approvals showing no maintenance add-on.
comments: 2024-11-15 10:12 - Aisha Khan (Support): Created ticket after customer raised invoice dispute. Attached invoice PDF and screenshot of product settings indicating no maintenance add-on enabled.
2024-11-15 11:05 - Miguel Ortega (Billing Eng): Acknowledged. Pulling postback logs and checking postback-to-ledger mapping. Assigned to billing and infra to triage routing events around 2024-10-29.

2024-11-16 09:40 - SRE (Lena Fischer): Found routing anomaly where router returned 'hosted-fallback' tag for a subset of requests from nimbleretail project between 03:42–03:54 UTC. Opening INT-2123 for deeper router/scheduler traces.

2024-11-16 13:22 - Billing (Miguel Ortega): Postback audit shows a SKU remap step that maps 'fallback_maint_sku' to private-maintenance when the request origin header is 'private' AND pinged during maintenance-eligible window. Need to confirm why window was marked eligible.

2024-11-17 08:10 - Customer (NimbleRetail - Elena Park): Customer confirms they did not schedule maintenance and no internal ticket authorized any add-on. Asks for immediate provisional credit while investigation continues.

2024-11-18 16:30 - Billing (Miguel Ortega): Applied provisional credit equal to surcharge amount to customer's account pending root cause (credit id CR-2024-11-18-246999). Notified finance. Will follow with permanent fix if rule misapplied.

2024-11-19 12:00 - SRE (Lena Fischer): Root cause identified in scheduler: a rebalance operation set an 'autoscale_maintenance' flag for the impacted machine group for 2024-10-29 03:40–04:00 UTC. That flag erroneously propagated to router metadata which later flagged requests as maintenance-eligible during billing aggregation. Patch deployed to stop flag propagation (PR linked).
investigation_notes: Timeline reconstruction: routing anomaly -> flagged as maintenance-eligible -> billing postback mapping applied maintenance SKU. Key findings: (1) scheduler rebalance toggled an internal 'autoscale_maintenance' marker when performing ephemeral node drain. (2) router augmented request metadata with that marker for in-flight requests due to a race in the metadata refresh path. (3) the billing postback remap logic interprets presence of 'autoscale_maintenance' on a private origin as justification to apply maintenance surcharge SKU. The behavior is legal for planned customer maintenance but not for internal autoscaler operations. Related PR fixes router metadata propagation (https://github.com/redwood/router/pull/789) and billing rule hardened to require explicit customer opt-in for maintenance SKUs (https://github.com/redwood/billing/pull/4187).
resolution: Provisional credit applied on 2024-11-18 (CR-2024-11-18-246999). Permanent fix deployed: router metadata propagation patched and billing remap rules updated to require explicit maintenance purchase flag. Finance notified and invoice adjusted; customer notified of credit and claim closure plan. Recommended follow-ups: retro-audit all invoices during 2024-10-29 window for customers with private deployments to ensure no other inadvertent maintenance surcharges were applied.
